mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 0.5% month-over-month signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL increases do not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE drops below 4% do not correlate with subsequent inflationary pressures.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals robust consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in expansionary demand periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant decline in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 2% month-over-month signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO declines do not correlate with subsequent negative market reactions.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.3% month-over-month, the combined effect signals tightening monetary conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combined conditions do not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000, the combined effect signals a tightening labor market with wage inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: tight labor market with wage inflation
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combined conditions do not correlate with subsequent inflationary pressures.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals a robust housing market, which boosts related sectors and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in expansionary housing market periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When Industrial Production (INDPRO) is below 100 and the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 1.5%, the combined effect signals a supply-side slowdown with tightening monetary conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: supply-side slowdown with tightening monetary conditions
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combined conditions do not correlate with subsequent negative market reactions.
